title: Think: A Compelling Introduction to Philosophy
author: Simon Blackburn

body.start_marker: Introduction This book is for people who want to think

translation.context: An introductory philosophy book for the general reader, written by an analytic philosopher. It works through knowledge, scepticism, the mind-body problem, free will, personal identity, God, reasoning and logic, the external world, and ethics, discussing Descartes, Hume, Kant, Berkeley, Locke, Leibniz, Wittgenstein and others. The prose is argumentative, precise and often ironic: thought experiments, dialectical objections and replies, and technical terms used with exact meaning.
translation.instructions: Philosophical terms are technical: translate them with their established Italian philosophical equivalents, consistently across the whole book, never with everyday synonyms. Quote established Italian renderings of classic formulas where they exist (e.g. 'Cogito, ergo sum' left in Latin, 'genio maligno' for Descartes's evil demon). Keep the author's ironic, conversational register: he addresses the reader directly and uses humour; do not flatten it into academic prose. Preserve the structure of arguments — premises, objections, replies — without paraphrasing or shortening. Do not translate names of philosophers or work titles that are conventionally cited in the original, but use the established Italian title when one exists (e.g. 'Meditazioni metafisiche').
